post.caption:
A GPS satellite does not know where you are. It broadcasts its identity and the time, your receiver measures how late the signal is, and four of those pin you to a point while also correcting your phone's own clock. Which makes the whole thing a clock comparison, and the clocks disagree: weaker gravity up there speeds them up, orbital speed slows them down, and gravity wins by roughly 38 microseconds a day. Without the correction the fix drifts kilometres off within a day.
